messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: measuring distances when horizon is not available
parts:
A clinometer will work at very close distances but once the angle is
smallish (<5 degrees) they aren't very useful. A less expensive laser
range finder will do better than a clinometer. Alternatively if you can
get the distance to the iceberg (radar?)at the time of the measurement
you can still use it in place of the horizon distance with reticle
binoculars.

--jeff

We were thinking of using laser range finders but considering the time the traget stays in view, the distance from the ship and the sea state, we would need a military grade laser range finder and our budget does not allow this kind of device. I was wondering if the use of a clinometer would work since it seems the horizon is not necessarily needed, compared to reticulated binos.
